newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia minister says mining changes not final.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia minister says mining changes not final.

text.p: Indonesian Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said on Monday proposed changes to the country's mining regulations were not final.

"They are still being discussed at the lower levels (of the ministry). They have not come to me yet," he told reporters after a meeting of economic ministers ahead of the regular monthly cabinet meeting on Wednesday.
Sudjana's remarks follows proposals by his ministry for sweeping changes to the seventh-generation contracts of work which are crucial for mining companies.
The proposals include requiring foreign mining companies to allocate at least a 10 percent free stake to the government in future mining ventures.
When asked about current laws that allow 100 percent foreign owned companies to operate in Indonesia, Sudjana said: "We will just follow the law."
Under the proposals, mining companies with operations in Indonesia will have to share capital gains made on stock exchanges outside the country with their shareholders.
In addition, raising of additional capital through a public offering of shares must be done in Indonesia.
The ministry had given mining companies until Tuesday to respond to the proposals, which a number of mining analysts said could jeopardise foreign investment in Indonesia.
